note: Every sound in The Whispering Spring. All of it is a placeholder until the artist supplies files: set an entry's "file" to its URL (under /whispering-spring/audio/) and audio.js plays the recording instead of the placeholder recipe. Titles, lyrics and transcripts marked placeholder are stand-ins too.

spring.phrase1.caption: The water answers: a low ringing note.

spring.phrase2.caption: A second answer: three notes rising.

spring.phrase3.caption: The spring sings: a single piano line (placeholder for the isolated vocal phrase).

cairn.chord.caption: The cairn plays the chord you stacked.

ribbon.tie.caption: The ribbon is tied. It catches the wind.

ribbon.tie.bell.caption: The ribbon is tied; its bell rings as it catches the wind.

stone.flat.caption: The flat stone sounds a low D.

stone.long.caption: The long stone sounds an A.

stone.round.caption: The round stone sounds an F sharp.

stone.wedge.caption: The wedge stone sounds an E, the ninth.

stone.pebble.caption: The pebble sounds a high C sharp, the seventh.

extras.title: Handwritten lyric
extras.text:
(Placeholder lyric — the artist's handwritten page goes here.)

I came down to the water
where the cedar roots let go,
and it answered me in three words
I was too still to know.

extras.title: Voice note
extras.transcript: (Placeholder transcript — the artist's voice note will be transcribed here.) This one started on a walk by the creek. I tied a ribbon for someone I miss, and the song is what the wind did with it.

voice.note: What the quail says, in the musician's own voice. Placeholder lines until the artist writes theirs. Each plays with the quail's babble voice; a line with a "file" plays that recording instead.
greeting: Welcome to the spring, friend. Sit a while; the water remembers every song.
You found your way here. Listen close, and the grove will share a few songs with you.
prayers: May the water keep you, and the wind carry what you cannot.
For every tired heart that finds this place: rest here, and go on lighter.
Bless the roots that hold the bank, and the hands that tie the ribbons.
May you hear your own song in the quiet.
ribbon: I will keep watch over that one. May the wind carry it home.
Tied with care. The tree holds it now, and so do I.
found_all: You have heard everything the grove had to give. Come back whenever you need the quiet.
